terminalSequence.text: # 3rd year CSE @ University of Asia Pacific
# building things that need to hold up

paragraphs: I'm a third-year, first-semester CSE student at the University of Asia Pacific, and I've been at it since 2024. My coursework and side projects both circle the same question: how do you build software that actually holds up — correct under load, and hard to break into.

That question pulls me toward three areas in particular: systems programming close to the machine, defensive security practices that anticipate misuse, and database design that keeps data honest. I like problems where the constraints are real, not theoretical.

values.title: Code quality
values.description: Readable, tested code over clever code. I'd rather ship something maintainable than something merely working.

values.title: Security first
values.description: I think about failure modes and misuse cases while designing, not after something breaks.

values.title: Honest learning
values.description: I label what I know, what I'm still learning, and what I've only read about — no inflated claims.

values.title: Collaboration
values.description: Good software is a team effort. I write for the next person reading the code, including future me.

items.title: Algorithms
items.description: Push DSA fluency further — timed problem sets, and applying patterns to real project code instead of isolated exercises.

items.title: Systems programming
items.description: Get comfortable building small C/C++ pipelines end-to-end — memory management, build systems, and performance basics.

items.title: Full-stack
items.description: Ship a complete end-to-end web app, from schema to UI, to connect the database and web skills I'm building separately.

items.title: Cybersecurity automation
items.description: Write Python tooling for log analysis and scan-report parsing — automating the repetitive parts of defensive work.

goals.note: Alongside coursework, I'm looking to contribute to open-source projects and take on an internship where I can apply these skills on real systems.
